fullPassage:
Whose Side Are You on?

Should social media have a "Dislike" button?

Charlie
One possible benefit of a "Dislike" button is that it would let people disagree with or be unhappy with a post without having to say something bad about it. This could help make conversations on social media platforms more open, honest, and respectful. A "Dislike" button could also help figure out what users like or find useful. By letting people express what they don't like about a post, content creators can get useful feedback and learn what their audience likes and doesn't like.

Jimin
The "Dislike" button can definitely be a useful tool to measure online engagement, but there are more negative effects than the positive. The presence of "Dislike" buttons and other negative replies illustrates how unfriendly social media can be. Many businesses directly ask for "5-star" ratings because anything less may actually hurt their reputation. A "Dislike" button encourages users to take advantage of the system rather than provide an honest opinion. While it may be useful for creators, it can also be harmful to both them and everyone else.

Is it okay to regift?

Lucia
Many gifts are thoughtful and personalized for the receiver. However, with online shopping apps and convenience stores everywhere, many gifts are also given just so that the giver isn't caught empty-handed. I don't see a problem with regifting common gifts until they find a home with someone who will appreciate them. The giving of the gift is the thoughtful gesture, not the actual gift itself. For this reason, you shouldn't feel guilty about regifting something that might be thrown away.

Richard
I don't think regifting is a good thing. A gift is something you receive from someone who put thought and effort into it. A gift is more than just an item. It contains the giver's feelings for the receiver. Something like that shouldn't just be given away to another person. Also, if the original giver finds out that their gift was given away, it could cause hard feelings. All in all, I don't think regifting is worth the trouble that it could cause. Just keep the gift as a reminder of a good relationship.

questions.passage: One possible benefit of a "Dislike" button is that it would let people (A)[disagree / agree] with or be unhappy with a post without having to say something bad about it. This could help make conversations on social media platforms more open, (B)[honest / hostile], and respectful. A "Dislike" button could also help figure out what users like or find (C)[useful / useless].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 싫어요 버튼으로 반대할 수 있고, 대화를 더 정직하게, 사용자가 유용하다고 느끼는 것을 파악할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① disagree — honest — useful
❌ ② agree — honest — useless
❌ ③ disagree — hostile — useless
❌ ④ agree — hostile — useful
✅ (A) disagree: 싫어요 버튼의 기능. (B) honest: open, respectful과 병렬. (C) useful: 유용한 것을 파악.
det.tip: disagree(반대하다) ↔ agree(동의하다). honest(정직한) ↔ hostile(적대적인). useful(유용한) ↔ useless(쓸모없는).

questions.passage: The "Dislike" button can definitely be a useful tool to measure online engagement, but there are more (A)[negative / positive] effects than the positive. The presence of "Dislike" buttons and other negative replies (B)[illustrates / eliminates] how unfriendly social media can be. A "Dislike" button encourages users to take (C)[advantage / care] of the system rather than provide an honest opinion.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 부정적 효과가 더 많다. 싫어요 버튼은 소셜미디어가 얼마나 비우호적인지 보여준다. 시스템을 이용하게 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① negative — illustrates — advantage
❌ ② positive — illustrates — care
❌ ③ negative — eliminates — care
❌ ④ positive — eliminates — advantage
✅ (A) negative: 긍정보다 부정 효과가 더 많음. (B) illustrates: 보여줌. (C) advantage: take advantage of = 이용하다.
det.tip: take advantage of(이용하다) vs take care of(돌보다). illustrate(보여주다) vs eliminate(제거하다).

questions.passage: Many gifts are (A)[thoughtful / thoughtless] and personalized for the receiver. However, with online shopping apps and convenience stores everywhere, many gifts are also given just so that the giver isn't caught (B)[empty-handed / red-handed]. I don't see a problem with regifting common gifts until they find a home with someone who will (C)[appreciate / abandon] them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 많은 선물은 사려 깊고 개인화된다. 선물 주는 사람이 빈손으로 잡히지 않기 위해. 감사히 여길 사람에게 줄 때까지.
det.analysis:
✅ ① thoughtful — empty-handed — appreciate
❌ ② thoughtless — empty-handed — abandon
❌ ③ thoughtful — red-handed — abandon
❌ ④ thoughtless — red-handed — appreciate
✅ (A) thoughtful: personalized와 병렬, 사려 깊은. (B) empty-handed: 빈손으로 잡히다. (C) appreciate: 감사히 여기다.
det.tip: empty-handed(빈손의) vs red-handed(현행범의). thoughtful(사려 깊은) vs thoughtless(무심한). appreciate(감사하다) vs abandon(버리다).

questions.passage: I don't think regifting is a good thing. A gift is something you receive from someone who put thought and effort into it. A gift is more than just an item. It contains the giver's ①<u>feelings</u> for the receiver. Something like that shouldn't just be ②<u>given away</u> to another person. Also, if the original giver finds out that their gift was given away, it could cause ③<u>hard</u> feelings. All in all, I don't think regifting is ④<u>worth</u> the joy that it could cause.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 리기프팅은 그것이 야기할 수 있는 문제(trouble)만큼의 가치가 없다. joy(기쁨)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①feelings: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②given away: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③hard: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④worth the joy: 원문은 worth the trouble. 리기프팅의 부정적 맥락에서 joy는 모순.
det.tip: trouble(문제, 곤란) ↔ joy(기쁨). 반대 주장의 맥락을 파악.

questions.passage: The "Dislike" button can definitely be a useful tool to measure online engagement, but there are more negative effects than the positive. The presence of "Dislike" buttons and other negative replies illustrates how ①<u>unfriendly</u> social media can be. Many businesses directly ask for "5-star" ratings because anything less may actually ②<u>hurt</u> their reputation. A "Dislike" button ③<u>encourages</u> users to take advantage of the system rather than ④<u>provide</u> a dishonest opinion.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 시스템을 이용하게 하고 정직한(honest) 의견을 제공하지 않게 한다. dishonest(부정직한)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①unfriendly: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②hurt: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③encourages: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④dishonest: 원문은 honest. 'rather than provide an honest opinion'에서 honest가 맞음.
det.tip: honest(정직한) ↔ dishonest(부정직한). 시스템 이용 vs 정직한 의견 제공의 대조.

questions.passage: Many gifts are thoughtful and ①<u>personalized</u> for the receiver. However, with online shopping apps and convenience stores everywhere, many gifts are also given just so that the giver isn't caught ②<u>empty-handed</u>. I don't see a problem with regifting common gifts until they find a home with someone who will ③<u>appreciate</u> them. The giving of the gift is the thoughtful ④<u>obstacle</u>, not the actual gift itself.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선물을 주는 행위가 사려 깊은 행동(gesture)이다. obstacle(장애물)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①personalized: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②empty-handed: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③appreciate: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④obstacle: 원문은 gesture(행동, 제스처). 선물 주기가 '장애물'이면 맥락 모순.
det.tip: gesture(행동, 몸짓) ↔ obstacle(장애물). 'thoughtful gesture'은 '사려 깊은 행동'.

questions.passage: One possible benefit of a "Dislike" button is that it would let people disagree with or be unhappy with a post without having to say something bad about it. This could help make conversations on social media platforms more open, honest, and __________. A "Dislike" button could also help figure out what users like or find useful. By letting people express what they don't like about a post, content creators can get useful feedback and learn what their audience likes and doesn't like.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 대화를 더 개방적이고, 정직하고, 존중하는 것으로 만들 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③respectful: open, honest와 병렬로 긍정적 형용사. ❌ ①aggressive(공격적): 반대. ❌ ②anonymous(익명의): 맥락 무관. ❌ ④competitive(경쟁적): 무관.
det.tip: open, honest, respectful: 모두 긍정적 소통의 형용사.

questions.passage: The "Dislike" button can definitely be a useful tool to measure online engagement, but there are more negative effects than the positive. The presence of "Dislike" buttons and other negative replies illustrates how unfriendly social media can be. Many businesses directly ask for "5-star" ratings because anything less may actually hurt their __________. A "Dislike" button encourages users to take advantage of the system rather than provide an honest opinion. While it may be useful for creators, it can also be harmful to both them and everyone else.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 5점 미만은 평판을 해칠 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④reputation: 별점이 낮으면 평판에 해. ❌ ①creativity(창의성): 무관. ❌ ②efficiency(효율): 무관. ❌ ③audience(청중): hurt 목적어로 어색.
det.tip: reputation: 평판, 명성. 'hurt one's reputation' = 평판을 해치다.

questions.passage: A gift is something you receive from someone who put thought and effort into it. A gift is more than just an item. It contains the giver's feelings for the receiver. Something like that shouldn't just be given away to another person. Also, if the original giver finds out that their gift was given away, it could cause __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 원래 선물한 사람이 알면 서운한 감정을 유발할 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①hard feelings: 원문 그대로. 리기프팅 발각 → 서운함. ❌ ②great joy: 반대. ❌ ③new friendships: 무관. ❌ ④mutual respect: 무관.
det.tip: hard feelings: 서운한 감정, 악감정. cause hard feelings = 감정을 상하게 하다.

questions.passage: The presence of "Dislike" buttons and other negative replies <u>illustrates</u> how unfriendly social media can be.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'illustrates'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 소셜미디어가 얼마나 비우호적인지 보여준다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②shows: illustrate ≈ show(보여주다). ❌ ①hides(숨기다): 반대. ❌ ③prevents(막다): 무관. ❌ ④increases(증가시키다): 무관.
det.tip: illustrate: 예시로 보여주다, 설명하다. ≈ show, demonstrate.

questions.passage: I don't see a problem with regifting common gifts until they find a home with someone who will <u>appreciate</u> them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'appreciate'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 감사히 여길 사람에게 갈 때까지.
det.analysis: ✅ ③value: appreciate ≈ value(가치 있게 여기다). ❌ ①admire(존경하다): 감탄의 의미는 있으나 '감사히 여기다'와 다름. ❌ ②recognize(인식하다): 가치를 안다는 점에서 유사하나 '감사'의 뜻 없음. ❌ ④tolerate(참다): 수용의 의미가 있으나 감사와 다름.
det.tip: appreciate: 감사하다, 가치를 알다. ≈ value, be grateful for. admire(존경하다)와 tolerate(참다)는 의미가 다름.

questions.passage: A "Dislike" button encourages users to take advantage of the system rather than <u>provide</u> an honest opinion.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'provide'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 정직한 의견을 제공하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①offer: provide ≈ offer(제공하다). ❌ ②withdraw(철회): 반대. ❌ ③demand(요구): 다른 의미. ❌ ④reject(거부): 반대.
det.tip: provide: 제공하다. ≈ offer, supply, give.

questions.passage: A "Dislike" button encourages users to take advantage of the system rather than provide an honest opinion. While it may be useful for creators, it can also be <u>harmful</u> to both them and everyone else.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'harmful'과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 창작자에게 유용할 수 있지만, 그들과 모두에게 해로울 수도 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②beneficial: harmful(해로운)의 반의어. 유익한. ❌ ①dangerous(위험한): 동의어. ❌ ③damaging(손해를 주는): 동의어. ❌ ④destructive(파괴적인): 동의어.
det.tip: harmful(해로운) ↔ beneficial(유익한). 나머지 3개는 모두 harmful과 유사.

questions.passage: Many gifts are <u>thoughtful</u> and personalized for the receiver. However, with online shopping apps and convenience stores everywhere, many gifts are also given just so that the giver isn't caught empty-handed.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'thoughtful'과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 사려 깊은 선물 ↔ 부주의한.
det.analysis: ✅ ④careless: thoughtful(사려 깊은)의 반의어. ❌ ①considerate(배려 깊은): 동의어. ❌ ②caring(돌보는): 유사. ❌ ③generous(관대한): 유사.
det.tip: thoughtful(사려 깊은) ↔ careless(부주의한, 생각 없는).

questions.passage:
(A) By letting people express what they don't like about a post, content creators can get useful <u>feedback</u> and learn what their audience likes and doesn't like.

(B) I don't see a <u>problem</u> with regifting common gifts until they find a home with someone who will appreciate them.
questions.stem: (A)의 'feedback'과 (B)의 'problem'의 의미를 가장 잘 나타낸 것은?

det.korean: (A) 유용한 의견/피드백을 받을 수 있다. (B) 리기프팅에 문제점이 없다고 본다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 반응 — (B) 질문
✅ ② (A) 의견 — (B) 문제점
❌ ③ (A) 보상 — (B) 해결책
❌ ④ (A) 의견 — (B) 질문
✅ ② (A)의견: creators가 audience 취향을 '배울 수 있는 의견'. (B)문제점: '문제가 없다'에서의 problem.
det.tip: feedback: ①기술적 피드백 ②의견/반응. problem: ①수학 문제 ②문제점/어려움.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the opinion that people have about how good or bad someone or something is"

det.korean: "사람이나 사물이 얼마나 좋은지 나쁜지에 대한 사람들의 의견" = 평판.
det.analysis: ✅ ③reputation: 평판, 명성. 정의와 일치. ❌ ①engagement(참여): 무관. ❌ ②advantage(이점): 무관. ❌ ④gesture(행동): 무관.
det.tip: reputation: 평판. 본문 'hurt their reputation'에서 등장.

questions.passage: Many gifts are thoughtful and personalized for the receiver. However, with online shopping apps and convenience stores everywhere, many gifts are also given just so that the giver isn't caught empty-handed.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

Her __________ (person) approach to teaching made every student feel special.

det.korean: 그녀의 개인화된/개인적인 교육 방식이 모든 학생을 특별하게 느끼게 했다.
det.analysis: ✅ personalized 또는 personal: 명사 approach를 수식하는 형용사 필요. person → personalized/personal.
det.tip: person(명사) → personal(형용사)/personalized(형용사: 개인화된).

questions.passage: The presence of "Dislike" buttons and other negative replies illustrates how unfriendly social media can be. Many businesses directly ask for "5-star" ratings because anything less may actually hurt their reputation.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

The negative comments on the video __________ (illustration) how divided public opinion was on the issue.

det.korean: 영상의 부정적 댓글이 여론이 얼마나 나뉘었는지 보여주었다.
det.analysis: ✅ illustrated: 주어 comments(과거 맥락), 동사 필요. illustration(명사) → illustrate(동사) → illustrated(과거형).
det.tip: illustration(명사: 삽화/예시) → illustrate(동사: 보여주다) → illustrated(과거형).

questions.passage: I don't think regifting is a good thing. A gift is something you receive from someone who put thought and effort into it. A gift is more than just an item. It contains the giver's feelings for the receiver. Something like that shouldn't just be __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선물은 주는 사람의 감정이 담긴 것. 그냥 다른 사람에게 줘버리면 안 된다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②given away to another person: 원문 그대로. 리기프팅 반대 근거. ❌ ①kept forever: 원문에 없음. ❌ ③displayed: 무관. ❌ ④returned: 무관.
det.tip: give away: (공짜로) 줘버리다. 리기프팅의 핵심 행위.

questions.passage: One possible benefit of a "Dislike" button is that it would let people disagree with or be unhappy with a post without having to say something bad about it. This could help make conversations on social media platforms more open, honest, and respectful. A "Dislike" button could also help figure out what users like or find useful. By letting people express what they don't like about a post, content creators can get useful feedback and __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: learn what their audience likes and doesn't like

det.korean: 피드백을 받아 청중이 무엇을 좋아하고 싫어하는지 배울 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 원문 그대로. feedback을 통한 학습. ❌ ①: 댓글 삭제 아님. ❌ ②: 팔로워 증가 아님. ❌ ④: 논쟁 회피 아님.
det.tip: feedback → learn: 피드백의 목적은 청중 선호도 파악.
